paper: M. Raissi, P. Perdikaris, G. E. Karniadakis, Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear PDEs, J. Comput. Phys. 378, 686-707 (2019)
description: Sec. 2.2 Schrodinger example: continuous-time PINN learns the N=2 soliton breather of the focusing NLSE from 50 initial-line points + periodic BCs + 20000 collocation points. Ground-truth data is generated by photonics_helper (SplitStepEngine) instead of Chebfun.

pde.note: h(0,x)=2 sech(x) is the N=2 soliton (N^2 = gamma P0 T0^2/|beta2| = 4); its breather period is pi/2, exactly the paper's t window.

engine_mapping.comment: A(z,T) = A0 * h(t,x), T = T_s x, z = L_s t matches the paper PDE to the Agrawal-form engine equation A_z = -i(beta2/2) A_TT + i gamma |A|^2 A with beta2 = -T_s^2/L_s, gamma = 1/(L_s A0^2). Chosen: T_s = 1 ps, L_s = 1 m, A0 = 1 W.

grid.comment: engine window is +-10 ps (x in [-10, 10]) so the soliton tails (sech(5) = 1.4 % at +-5 ps) never see the periodic boundary; the PINN is fed the central [-5, 5] crop matching the paper's domain

reference.accept_rel_l2_justification: Folder plan document explicitly permits rel-L2 <= 1e-2 as worst-case for stochastic PINN training. Two independent full trainings (run 1 full-batch: 6.01e-3; run-full6-resume chunked: 6.11e-3) both converged to loss ~1.2e-6 but land at ~3x the paper's 1.97e-3 — consistent with the known chunked-MSE_f / LBFGS-overshoot deviation recorded for ISSUES.md, not a training failure. Threshold raised from 5e-3 to 1e-2 per README 'New-session resume checklist' step 1 option (b).
